docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Directed Evolution Monitoring & Analytics Portal is a web-based platform for staging and analysing directed evolution (DE) experiments.

This help manual explains how to: - Set up an analysis. - Upload and validate your data. - Interpret analytical outputs, including the Activity Score.

docs.title: What this portal does
docs.text: The portal supports the full workflow from experiment setup to ranked variant outputs. It can: - Retrieve details of the wild-type protein from UniProt. - Validate uploaded plasmid FASTA and experimental run files. - Compute a unified metric for Activity used to compare variants. - Tracks mutations across generations. - Identifies the best performing variants.

docs.title: Directed evolution context
docs.text:
In this project, DE runs in iterative cycles of mutagenesis, selection, and carry-forward of top variants. The portal is used after each experimental run to: - register the target protein using a UniProt accession code; - upload plasmid FASTA encoding the target polymerase; - upload assay output from the run (for example, DNA and protein quantification, used for selection); - identify the best performing variants and track performance across generations.

This keeps experimental records, sequence context, and results in one place during multi-generation studies.

docs.title: Who this manual is for
docs.text: This guide is for new users of the web portal, including students and researchers running directed evolution campaigns that can be easily monitored and analysed with this tool.

docs.title: Data Analysis
docs.text: This page explains analysis logic used by the portal, with emphasis on the Activity Metric.

docs.title: Analysis pipeline summary
docs.text: At a high level, the portal: 1. Ingests validated plasmid and wt protein sequences, with DE experimental run data 2. Applies preprocessing and quality-control rules. 3. Calculates a single Activity Metric for every variant. 4. Ranks variants and produces several visualisations to highlight analysis..

docs.title: What file formats are supported?
docs.text: The portal supports TSV and JSON inputs that match the required schema.

docs.title: Do I need a UniProt accession?
docs.text: Yes. The portal uses the UniProt accession to fetch and validate against the wild-type reference.

docs.title: Do I also need plasmid FASTA data?
docs.text: Yes. Upload plasmid FASTA encoding the variants from your DE run so sequence-level checks and downstream tracking can be performed.

docs.title: What does the Activity Metric represent?
docs.text: It is a composite score used to compare variants based on analysis components defined in Data Analysis.

docs.title: The full formula and logic are intentionally kept as a template until the final implementation details are available.
Can I export results?
docs.text: Yes, ranked outputs and summary tables can be exported for reporting.

docs.title: Why was my dataset rejected?
docs.text: Most rejections are due to schema mismatch, missing required values, or invalid sequence formatting. Validation checks occurs at every data upload point, specifying any issue to users.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page helps first-time users complete their first successful analysis run.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using the portal, ensure you have: - Registered an account for the platform. - A valid UniProt accession for the target wildtype protein from your research. - Input files in one of the supported formats (.tsv or .json).

docs.title: Recommended first run
docs.text:
1. Sign in to the portal.
  2. Create a new experiment.
  3. Enter target metadata, including the UniProt accession.
  4. Upload plasmid FASTA for the run.
  5. Upload the data from your experimental run (.tsv or .json) containing assay outputs, DNA sequences and variant identifiers.
  6. Resolve validation warnings or errors (if there are any present).
  7. Run analysis and review the generated outputs, which can be saved as a PDF.

docs.title: Input data expectations
docs.text: Document your real schema here. Typical fields include: - Variant ID. - Sequence DNA. - Round/generation label for every variant. - Raw DNA and protein abundances for every variant. - Optional metadata.

docs.title: Supported files
docs.text:
• TSV: tab-separated text with a header row.
  • JSON: array/object format, structured as key/value pairs.

docs.title: Access and permissions
docs.text: Describe role behavior in your portal: - Viewer: read-only results access. - Editor: upload and run analysis. - Admin: manage experiments and users.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Use this page to quickly diagnose common user issues.

docs.title: Unsupported file type
docs.text:
Symptom: - Upload fails immediately.

Fix: - Use .tsv or .json files only.

docs.title: Missing required fields
docs.text:
Symptom: - Validation reports missing columns/keys.

Fix: - Ensure required fields are present and named exactly as expected.

docs.title: Invalid sequence characters
docs.text:
Symptom: - Rows flagged for illegal symbols.

Fix: - Remove non-biological characters and whitespace. - Confirm DNA/protein alphabet expected by your pipeline.

docs.title: Length mismatch
docs.text:
Symptom: - Sequence length check fails.

Fix: - Verify target region and alignment with reference/wild-type.

docs.title: No Activity Metric generated
docs.text:
Symptom: - Analysis completes with empty score column.

Fix: - Check for missing activity inputs. - Confirm preprocessing did not filter all rows.

docs.title: Unexpected ranking
docs.text:
Symptom: - High-performing known variants rank low.

Fix: - Review normalisation method and metric weights. - Verify replicate handling and outlier rules.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text: If errors persist, share: - Experiment ID. - Timestamp of run. - Input schema/sample rows. - Full validation error text.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: This section documents the core end-to-end portal workflow.

docs.title: 0. Complete a DE experimental cycle (laboratory stage)
docs.text:
Before upload, a DE cycle is performed in the laboratory: - Variant libraries are generated by mutagenesis. - Variants are screened and selected based on assay performance. - Top-performing variants are carried forward to the next generation. This is usually quantified using DNA and protein abundance.

The droplets/variants are then profiled, sequenced, and prepared for upload to the portal.

docs.title: 1. Register experiment in the portal
docs.text:
Create an experiment record and provide: - Target protein name. - UniProt accession. - Optional campaign notes.

Expected system behaviour: - Portal fetches wild-type sequence and relevant annotations. - Metadata is stored for downstream validation and analysis.

docs.title: 2. Upload plasmid FASTA and run datasets
docs.text:
Upload: - plasmid FASTA data for the selected variants; - run data files (.tsv or .json) containing assay outputs and variant identifiers.

Expected system behaviour: - File format and schema are checked. - Required columns/keys are validated.

docs.title: 3. Validate sequences and measurements
docs.text:
Run validation checks before scoring.

Typical checks: - Invalid characters in sequences. - UniProt ID must match the wild-type - Polymerase DNA is not encoded a plasmid. - Missing activity values. And more.

docs.title: 4. Run analysis
docs.text: Start the analysis pipeline to produce: - Activity Scores. - Ranked variants table. - Generation/round-level summary statistics. - Mutation tracking And more.

docs.title: 5. Review and export outputs
docs.text: View the results, export them as a .pdf or .png: - Filter top variants. - Compare across rounds. - Export result tables for reporting.
